feat(post): wire_edm and sinker_edm machine kinds and the .mch edm section

Two declared-only machine kinds for the EDM family (#290 D1): wire
(X/Y, U/V for taper) and sinker (Z). The .mch file gains an optional
`edm` section - guide planes, max taper, wire diameters, AWT; orbit
patterns with the control's word, max orbit radius, pickup - absent
keys not stated, garbled ones refusing the file, the law restated in
is_sane for project files. No op family admits an EDM, and posting now
re-checks every op's family against its own setup's machine, so an op
made on a mill no longer posts after its setup is remounted onto steel
that cannot run it. Empty wire/sinker templates ship (no vendor
values), kept out of the picker until an EDM op exists.

Pinned by edm_machine (7 tests).

Fixes #530

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(post): the EDM templates are test fixtures until their posts ship

Every shipped .mch must be in the built-in library and every library
machine must have a post (machine_library); no EDM post exists until
#533 / #542, so the empty wire and sinker templates move to
crates/app/tests/edm/ and join the library with their kind's first post.

Refs #530

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(post): EDM condition table as user data in the .mch edm section

`edm.conditions[]`: the control's condition id, a name, the spark gap
per side, the wire diameter (wire) or electrode undersize (sinker), a
rough/skim/finish role and notes - the geometry a toolpath needs, never
the generator physics. Ids are required and unique, lengths scale with
the file's unit, a garbled entry refuses the file by its id, and
is_sane restates it for project files. Edm::condition(machine, id, need)
is the door an EDM op calls at command creation: a missing condition or
an unstated field it needs is refused by name. No conditions ship.

Pinned by edm_conditions (6 tests).

Fixes #531

feat(motion): wire EDM 2-axis contour generator - kerf offset to a stated side, start hole, corner minimum

The wire-centre path is the one closed profile's mitred parallel at the
kerf offset (wire radius + the condition's spark gap), inside it for a
die and outside it for a punch; a straight lead joins it to the stated
start hole and back. An inside corner or slot tighter than the offset,
a missing or misplaced start hole, an open, crossing or area-less
profile are refused by name. The moves ride one plane and state no pose
and no feed (#290 D2).

Refs #532

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(edm): Wire Contour operation - the machine's condition at the command door, no library tool, CL goldens

OpType::WireContour (id 41) in its own Wire EDM section and family,
admitted on a wire EDM only. The op names the machine condition it burns
with; CreateOperation / EditOperationParams refuse a missing condition,
gap or wire diameter by name (#531's door), and refuse a library tool on
a wire cut - the condition table is the wire's one source. The stamp
digests the condition's wire and gap, so an edited table re-marks the
cut Stale. Generation runs motion::wire_edm over the picked profile or
the model's through-silhouette. The machine check judges X/Y travel and
names what it does not judge; the post refuses a wire cut by name until
a wire post exists (#533).

Refs #532

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(edm): Wire Contour page fields, registry pins and the decision record

The UI's tab law draws every kind's sections, so the Wire Contour gets a
minimal page: side and start hole on Geometry, the workpiece planes on
Heights, the machine's conditions to choose from on Passes, no Feeds tab
(a wire cut states no feed). The ribbon tip names a wire EDM, not a
mill-turn, as the machine wire work needs. The registry's count pins
move to 42 kinds; the tool-law tests state the one family that mounts no
library tool. docs/decisions/532-wire-contour.md records what the
umbrella left open.

Fixes #532

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(post): generic ISO wire EDM post - RS-274 motion, every EDM code from the machine's edm.codes

assets/posts/wire-iso.cps ("Generic ISO Wire EDM") posts the 2-axis Wire
Contour: G0 to the start hole, AWT thread (or M00 for the operator),
condition select and compensation cancel from .mch edm.codes, the
wire-centre path in G1/G2/G3 X Y with no F, then wire cut and tip
disposal. A missing required code refuses by name ("machine <m> states
no edm.codes.<x>"); a non-wire_edm machine is refused by name.

- app: posting_wire streams the op's section (EdmCondition, WireSide);

- tests: wire_post.rs with a synthetic fixture (fictional FX- codes) and

Not exercised on a real EDM control (#290 D10).

feat(sim): wire EDM 2.5D verification - kerf, threading and slug laws block the post

A Wire Contour is judged at the post gate (posting_wire, beside the
plasma clause) against the part and the stock through the whole height
the vertical wire passes: a kerf nearer the product than wire radius +
gap is a gouge naming its move; a missing start hole, a path that no
longer starts at it, or a product within the kerf of the threading
point is refused; the pieces the closed cut frees are found by region
connectivity, and a die that drops the part or a punch that drops only
waste - or a cut that frees nothing - is refused. The report line names
what each cut frees. Decisions in docs/decisions/534-wire-verify.md.

Fixes #534

Merge issue/533-wire-iso-post into issue/534-wire-verify (posting_wire.rs, posting.rs, wire_contour.rs: keep both)

posting_wire.rs holds #533's Wire Contour stream (op_streams builds the

test(app): the wire laws stand between a wire cut and its NC text

On the combined #533/#534 head the wire post is real, so the wire
clause now gates actual NC text: a clean punch is judged by the wire
laws and posts wire-iso.cps's golden byte-for-byte (the program is
written, the not-judged line names the wire verdict); a die whose kerf
burns the plate above its 12 mm opening streams like any wire cut but
post_script refuses it by name ("Die1: wire gouge: the kerf of move
...") and writes no NC file.

Refs #534

feat(edm): wire tabs and the tab cut-off - the slug held until it is freed, an unheld slug refused

Tabs are off by default (#290 D6). When on, the count, the width, one
position per tab and the cut-off's condition are all stated; each
missing or impossible one is refused by name (width at or past the
side, a tab on a round's facets, overlapping tabs, a stretch the start
hole cannot reach, a cut-off condition on another kerf offset). The
main cut leaves the tabs (each run entered by its own lead, left back
along its own kerf); the cut-off follows as its own section with its
own condition after a program stop.

The hold law completes #534's slug law: a tabbed main cut must free
nothing and its cut-off frees the stated piece; an untabbed cut whose
slug drops is refused unless the op states a capture.

Fixes #539
